嫉.meaning: A <part>woman</part> knits her cat a sweater, but the cat runs off <part>rapidly</part> next door every time the neighbour opens a tin of tuna. She glares over the fence, needles clacking, green to the ears. She's <kanji>jealous</kanji> of a tin of fish.
嫉.on: She spies on them from behind a flapping bed <sound>sheet</sound> on the line.
嫉.kun: Next she knits it a <sound>so</sound>ck and a <sound>ne</sound>t hat, and the cat wears both next door.

諭.meaning: A young pilot flies loop-the-loops round the moon in the station's only <part>spaceship</part>, just for fun. The commander's voice crackles over the radio with a long, stern <part>speech</part> about fuel, safety and asking first. The pilot flies straight back, ears red. A firm but fair <kanji>rebuke</kanji>.
諭.on: To make peace afterwards, the commander leaves a <sound>yu</sound>zu on his seat.
諭.kun: He writes her a long <sound>sa</sound>ga of an apology and tapes a <sound>to</sound>ffee to the last page.

漸.meaning: <part>Water drops</part> fall from a warm, leaky tap onto a chocolate bunny, one at a time. No sudden <part>beheading</part> with a knife: the ears go first, then the head, drip by drip, all week. The bunny shrinks <kanji>steadily</kanji>.
漸.on: Its brown puddle trickles out into a raked <sound>zen</sound> garden.
漸.kun: A girl <sound>yo</sound>dels '<sound>Ya</sound>hoo!' when at last only the tail is left.

股.meaning: A <part>maiden</part> hiking all night under the <part>moon</part> keeps her map in a pocket strapped to her leg above the knee, so she can slap it out mid-stride. Her horse thinks she's patting it. Best place for a map: the <kanji>thigh</kanji>.
股.on: A sleepy <sound>ko</sound>ala rides in the pocket on her other leg.
股.kun: Her <sound>ma</sound>ma tucked a <sound>ta</sound>co in there for it too.

蓋.meaning: A picnicker sets a <part>dish</part> of jam tarts on the <part>grass</part>, turns round, and half are <part>gone</part>: wasps. She flips her sun hat over the rest and sits on it. Next time she'll bring a proper <kanji>cover</kanji>.
蓋.on: Her <sound>gui</sound>de dog lies across the hat to keep the wasps out.
蓋.kun: It even rests a <sound>foo</sound>t on her <sound>ta</sound>co box, like a lid.

某.meaning: Every night, someone hangs a <part>yoke</part> with two buckets of fresh milk on the <part>tree</part> at the crossroads, and nobody ever sees who. The villagers drink it and thank Mister Whatsit, You-Know-Who, or just <kanji>so-and-so</kanji>.
某.on: One night someone leaves a <sound>bou</sound>lder there instead, with a smiley face.
某.kun: Next, a <sound>so</sound>ck, <sound>re</sound>d and stuffed with <sound>ga</sound>rlic, hangs there for the <sound>shee</sound>p.

逝.meaning: Great-grandpa's last wish: <part>fold</part> his old letters into paper boats and set them on the <part>ramp</part> down to the river. One by one they slide into the water and drift off into the mist, as if waving goodbye for him. He has <kanji>departed</kanji>.
逝.on: In his old steel <sound>sa</sound>fe the family finds only more paper, for more boats.
逝.kun: A <sound>yu</sound>zu, his favourite fruit, floats after the boats.
